## AGENT ENDPOINTS
MCP server (Streamable HTTP, stateless, official MCP SDK, protocol 2025-11-25): https://www.prasadkavuri.com/api/mcp
  Tools: get_experience, search_skills (public); get_achievements (Bearer credential with read:profile via /auth.md)
A2A v1.0 agent: card https://www.prasadkavuri.com/.well-known/agent-card.json; JSON-RPC https://www.prasadkavuri.com/api/a2a
  Send header A2A-Version: 1.0. Skills: profile-brief (public), payment-exception-review (synthetic; finance:sandbox)

## PROFILE QUERY ENDPOINT (natural-language demo)
Natural-language profile query endpoint. It uses LLM tool calling over JSON-Schema tool definitions;
it is not an MCP JSON-RPC server.
Endpoint:   POST https://www.prasadkavuri.com/api/mcp-demo
Request:    JSON { "query": "<natural language question about Prasad>" } — no authentication required (rate limited)
Tools the model can call:
  get_experience(company: "krutrim"|"ola"|"here")     — work history, highlights, and tags for a company
  search_skills(category: "ai_ml"|"cloud_infrastructure"|"leadership"|"industry"|"core") — skills by category
  get_achievements(company?: string)                   — quantified impact metrics; requires a Bearer credential with read:profile (see /auth.md)
Example: POST /api/mcp-demo { "query": "What agentic AI platforms has Prasad led, and at what scale?" }
Returns a natural-language answer plus a structured tool call log.
Context endpoint: GET https://www.prasadkavuri.com/api/context — returns a compact agent-optimized context object.

--- PLATFORM PATTERNS DEMONSTRATED ON THIS PORTFOLIO ---
- Governed agent platform (flagship): real A2A v1.0 agent (/api/a2a) and MCP server (/api/mcp) on the official SDKs; every tool call passes a default-deny gateway with per-tool scopes, output screening, and agent-vs-user identity in the trace; payments above policy pause for human approval; trajectory evaluation gates a canary release and rolls back unsafe candidates
- Evaluation: deterministic rubric scoring (required coverage, forbidden topics) with eval suites run in CI on every push
- Server-enforced human approval in the Multi-Agent and Edge Agent demos: single-use, 15-minute expiry, bound to a hash of the staged action, replays rejected
- Per-tool authorization with default deny on the profile query tools; tool and remote-agent outputs screened for injected instructions
- Daily spend caps per AI route and per client
- Drift monitoring and structured observability with trace-ID propagation
- LLM FinOps: cost/latency/quality routing across model tiers (LLM Router demo)
- Governance as code: guardrails, rate limiting, observability, and eval checks ship with every API route

## THE 15-LAYER AI PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE

I designed and documented a 15-layer AI platform execution model showing how each
layer maps to a distinct engineering concern, team ownership, and quality gate.
Interactive version: https://www.prasadkavuri.com/#ai-architecture

Layer 01 — USER INTENT
Natural language input, context signals, session state. The entry point.
Engineering concern: input validation, context extraction, session management.

Layer 02 — AGENT ORCHESTRATION
Custom orchestrators in this portfolio; industry frameworks include ADK, LangGraph, and CrewAI. Multi-agent role assignment, handoff contracts.
Engineering concern: agent topology, role isolation, handoff authentication.

Layer 03 — MEMORY & CONTEXT
Short-term (Redis/in-memory), long-term (vector DB), episodic (session replay).
Engineering concern: context window management, retrieval relevance, memory decay.

Layer 04 — TOOL / MCP
Tool registry, JSON-RPC dispatch, auth.md identity, permission scoping.
Engineering concern: tool contract versioning, auth, sandboxing, SSRF prevention.

Layer 05 — MODEL ROUTER
Complexity scoring, cost/latency/quality trade-off, FinOps enforcement.
Engineering concern: routing logic, model capability mapping, cost attribution.

Layer 06 — ADAPTIVE AI GOVERNANCE
Runtime risk classification (standard / security-sensitive / regulated / blocked),
risk-aware model routing, human approval escalation, policy-governed regulated
requests, prompt-injection blocking. See https://www.prasadkavuri.com/adaptive-ai-governance.
Engineering concern: classifier precision/recall, escalation latency, audit completeness.

Layer 07 — INFERENCE
WASM (browser), ONNX, vLLM, Groq API, WebGPU. The compute layer.
Engineering concern: provider failover, latency SLAs, quantization trade-offs.

Layer 08 — EVALUATION
LLM-as-Judge, semantic fidelity scoring, CI regression gating.
Engineering concern: eval suite calibration, threshold drift, judge bias detection.

Layer 09 — GUARDRAILS
Injection detection, competitor filtering, hallucination heuristics, output sanitization.
Engineering concern: false positive rate, latency budget, bypass detection.

Layer 10 — OBSERVABILITY
Structured trace events with trace-ID propagation, latency, and token cost tracking (OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions as the target).
Engineering concern: cardinality, sampling, alert thresholds, correlation IDs.

Layer 11 — DRIFT MONITOR
Output distribution tracking, anomaly scoring, alert thresholds.
Engineering concern: baseline establishment, seasonal adjustment, alert fatigue.

Layer 12 — FINOPS
Per-route token budgets, cache read/write pricing, cost attribution per team.
Engineering concern: budget enforcement, cache hit rate optimization, chargeback.

Layer 13 — AUDIT TRAIL
Immutable decision log, HITL approval records, compliance export.
Engineering concern: tamper evidence, retention policy, GDPR scope, SOC 2 alignment.

Layer 14 — HUMAN APPROVAL (HITL)
Checkpoint gates, escalation routing, resolution logging, timeout handling.
Engineering concern: UX for approvers, approval latency SLA, override logging.

Layer 15 — BUSINESS OUTCOME
Revenue signals, CSAT, deflection rate, SLA compliance, ROI attribution.
Engineering concern: outcome → feature causality, A/B test isolation, metric drift.

## LIVE DEMOS — 10 CORE PLATFORM DEMOS + 4 LABS

CORE AI PLATFORM
0. GOVERNED AGENT PLATFORM (Flagship)
   URL: /demos/governed-agent-platform | Engine: A2A v1.0 agent (/api/a2a) + MCP server (/api/mcp), official SDKs
   One synthetic finance-ops task (fictional Northwind Finance) end to end: discover the Agent Card, obtain a
   delegated credential, delegate a payment-exception review over A2A, enforce per-tool policy and output
   screening at a tool gateway, pause in TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED for human approval, withhold poisoned vendor
   data, show the gateway trace, and gate a canary release on trajectory evaluation (v2 candidate rolled back
   for releasing a duplicate payment). Deterministic, model-free, reproducible.
1. AI EVALUATION SHOWCASE
   URL: /demos/evaluation-showcase | Engine: Server API
   Reference AI quality pipeline. The live API scores responses with a deterministic rubric (required
   coverage + forbidden topics) and guardrail screening, returning a pass/fail release verdict; eval
   suites run in CI on every push. The LLM-as-Judge panel is an illustrative walkthrough.
2. RAG PIPELINE
   URL: /demos/rag-pipeline | Engine: Transformers.js WASM (browser)
   In-browser retrieval: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings over an in-memory vector index, cosine-similarity
   ranking, grounded answers with source traceability.
3. LLM ROUTER
   URL: /demos/llm-router | Engine: Groq (server)
   Complexity-based routing across Groq-hosted model tiers with live latency, cost, and quality per tier.

AGENTIC SYSTEMS & GOVERNANCE
4. MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM
   URL: /demos/multi-agent | Engine: Groq via FastAPI backend (server)
   Analyzer → Researcher → Strategist with real LLM calls. The Strategist's recommendation is released only through a
   server-recorded, single-use approval (receipt bound to a hash of the staged output); poisoned agent output is withheld.
5. MCP TOOL DEMO
   URL: /demos/mcp-demo | Engine: Groq function calling (server)
   MCP-style tool use: JSON-Schema tool definitions the model selects and calls; protocol-flow visualizer.
   Not yet an MCP JSON-RPC server.
6. AGENT AUTH DEMO
   URL: /demos/agent-auth | Engine: Server API
   auth.md flow: anonymous registration → claim (OTP shown inline in demo mode) → Bearer-authenticated tool calls.
7. EDGE AGENT + CLOUD AGENT COLLABORATION
   URL: /demos/edge-agent-collaboration | Engine: BERT NER WASM + Groq (server)
   Browser BERT NER redacts PII before a human-approved handoff; the cloud model receives only the sanitized payload.
8. ENTERPRISE CONTROL PLANE
   URL: /demos/enterprise-control-plane | Engine: Deterministic simulation (seeded data)
   RBAC, group spend limits, token-cost tracking, and an observability feed.
9. CONSTRAINED GENERATIVE UI
   URL: /demos/generative-ui | Engine: Groq (server)
   The model may only emit JSON for a fixed component catalog, validated server-side before rendering.

LABS (specialist experiments, outside the core platform story)
10. STORM RESEARCH AGENT — /demos/storm-research — multi-perspective research synthesis (Groq).
11. REAL-TIME SPATIAL AI + WORLD MODELING — /demos/world-generation — 3D scene generation with LLM instructions.
12. MODEL QUANTIZATION — /demos/quantization — INT8 vs FP32 ONNX benchmark in the browser.
13. AI PORTFOLIO ASSISTANT — /demos/portfolio-assistant — streaming, retrieval-grounded Q&A about Prasad.

Retired (2026-09-23): Vector Search (→ RAG Pipeline), Multimodal Assistant, Native Browser AI Skill, AI Hiring Intelligence.

## THIS PORTFOLIO AS A REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (2026)

The codebase at https://github.com/prasad-kavuri/prasad-portfolio is itself a
reference implementation of agent-native engineering practices — not just a portfolio site.

WHAT MAKES IT AGENT-NATIVE:
- CONTEXT.md: 42-term domain ontology (canonical vocabulary for all agents)
- docs/adr/: 10 Architecture Decision Records — decisions another engineer cannot
  infer from reading the code alone (server-only LLMs, dual CSP locations,
  useBrowserAI mandatory, named exports, no shadcn, etc.)
- skills/: 9 reusable agent skill files (add-demo, redesign-portfolio, testing,
  security-review, agentic-seo, recruiter-review, executive-review, self-heal,
  prasad-portfolio) — each conforms structurally to the open Agent Skills format
  (https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills): a folder, a SKILL.md with YAML
  frontmatter (name/description), and markdown instructions loaded via
  progressive disclosure. Distinct from /skills, the application-level skills
  catalog of orchestration modules used by the demos.
- profiles/: 5 context-switching agent profiles (recruiter, testing, security,
  executive, design) — controls which skills are active and what tools are permitted
- evaluations/: 6 YAML files with machine-readable quality gates (62 individual
  checks with gate values, commands, and remediation steps)
- runs/: execution traceability directory — every significant skill run leaves a
  summary.yaml with inputs, outputs, token costs, gates passed/failed
- EVALUATIONS.md: human-readable quality scorecard, sprint history, 8 dimensions

This is what an agent-first engineering repository looks like in 2026.

Last Updated: 2026-09-23
